subject: Thank you for applying to QuinStreet
body:
Hi Netanya,

Thank you for applying to the Data Analyst  position. While this letter is automatically generated, our candidate review process is not. Here's what will happen next:

People, not robots read your resume. People who know about the position review each resume that is submitted to us.

Our goal is to have your resume reviewed within two weeks of submitting it to us.

If you're selected to move to the next stage of the interview process, a recruiter will reach out to conduct a preliminary phone screening.

If you're not selected for an interview, please know there are most likely several factors that influenced our decision. One major influencer is unfortunately out of your control - the strength of our candidate pool. Oftentimes, you may have good to great professional experience, but we have to send a rejection because of the level of competition for the role is so high.

Thank you again for submitting your resume for our review. We will make every effort to provide you with consistent communication during your candidacy with us, regardless of the outcome.

Please keep in mind, a QuinStreet Recruiter will never ask you to purchase equipment or ask for any personal information (ie - bank information, deposit checks, personal identity number, government identification) and will only receive email communication from our domains, @quinstreet.com and/or @us.greenhouse-mail.io.

subject: Re: Application Update: Schepmont Group - Data Analyst (Remote)
body:
Hello Netanya,

We're reaching out with another update regarding your application for the Data Analyst (Remote) position with Schepmont Group.

At this stage, our client has many internal candidates and several candidates presented by Schepmont Group moving forward to final interview steps. Given the confidence they have in these candidates as potential hires, they have decided to temporarily pause their search with us as they make their final evaluation.

We want to be transparent with you about that, while also letting you know that your application is still being kept on file and remains under consideration should the search reopen or expand again as the client continues through this growth phase.

Based on what we're seeing, there is a good chance that the current roles will be filled within the next few business days, and the timeline for additional needs in this department is unclear.
While we are happy to keep your information active on our side, we wanted to keep you informed to be respectful of your time. We would encourage you to continue your job search and not hold out for this Data Analyst (Remote) position.

In the current market, especially for technical roles like this, strong candidates tend to do best when they stay proactive and focus their time on openings that are moving quickly and are most likely to get to the offer phase.
One thing we continue to see is that many qualified applicants lose momentum not because they lack the technical background, but because they spend too much time in processes that are delayed, overcrowded, or not as active as they appear from the outside.

For that reason, continuing to search strategically and keeping yourself in front of the right kinds of openings is often the best move.

If this particular search resumes, or if the client opens additional roles that align with your background, we will absolutely keep you in mind and reach back out.

We appreciate your interest in the position and your patience throughout the process, and will continue to update you when we have a more clear direction from our client.

> In the meantime, we wanted to pass along some additional guidance that may help you not only in this process, but as you continue applying for other roles in the current market. One thing we are seeing across a very large number of applicants right now is that many candidates have enough technical ability to do the job, but far fewer present their background in a way that makes it immediately clear why they are the right fit during the interview process.
> 
> With that in mind, here are a few practical points that can help you strengthen the way you approach this role during the interview process, and as you continue your broader search:
> - Do not let your tools speak for themselves. Many analysts list SQL, Power BI, Tableau, Python, and Excel on their resume but never explain what they actually built or solved with them. Employers want to see the work, not the toolkit.
> - Anchor every project to a real outcome. If you built a dashboard, explain what decision it informed. If you ran an analysis, explain what changed because of it. Technical skill is common at this level. Showing that your analysis moved something measurable is what separates strong candidates from average ones.
> - Show range across the full analytics process. The strongest candidates can speak to data collection, cleaning, modeling, visualization, stakeholder communication, and follow-through. Even if your experience leans heavier in one of these areas, demonstrating awareness of the full picture makes you look more capable and more senior than your title might suggest.
> - Avoid the generic-resume trap. One of the biggest mistakes we see is resumes that read like they were sent to every analyst opening on the market with no adjustments. Even a strong background gets passed over when the language is too broad to match what a specific employer is actually trying to solve.
> - Make your cross-functional collaboration obvious. Data analyst roles, especially remote ones, succeed or fail on how well someone communicates and partners across teams. Concrete examples of working with operations, finance, product, or leadership go further than generic mentions of "collaboration."
> - Quantify your contributions wherever possible. Candidates consistently undersell their impact. If your work helped reduce reporting time, improve forecasting accuracy, increase visibility into a key metric, or surface an opportunity worth real money, that should be front and center, with numbers attached.
> - Recognize how much time gets wasted on the wrong opportunities. In the current market, a lot of strong analysts spend hours applying to roles that are stalled, overcrowded, or no longer a true priority for the company. Focusing your effort on roles that are clearly active and aligned is one of the highest-leverage things you can do during a search.
> - Practice explaining technical work in plain language. Many analysts can describe their work to other analysts but struggle when a hiring manager or executive asks them to walk through a project. If you can explain what you analyzed, why it mattered, and what changed because of it, in three or four clean sentences, you will outperform most of the other candidates you are competing with.
>

Hello Netanya,

We're reaching out with a new update regarding your application for the Data Analyst (Remote) position with Schepmont Group.

Firstly, we want to apologize for the slower than normal pace of this process. Given the volume of applications, the client's ongoing planning around additional hires for new departments and balance of interviewing internal candidates and candidates presented through Schepmont Group - things are moving a bit more gradually than we originally hoped. That said, our internal review process is still underway and your application remains in active consideration.

In the meantime, we wanted to pass along some additional guidance that may help you not only in this process, but as you continue applying for other roles in the current market. One thing we are seeing across a very large number of applicants right now is that many candidates have enough technical ability to do the job, but far fewer present their background in a way that makes it immediately clear why they are the right fit during the interview process.

With that in mind, here are a few practical points that can help you strengthen the way you approach this role during the interview process, and as you continue your broader search:
- Do not let your tools speak for themselves. Many analysts list SQL, Power BI, Tableau, Python, and Excel on their resume but never explain what they actually built or solved with them. Employers want to see the work, not the toolkit.
- Anchor every project to a real outcome. If you built a dashboard, explain what decision it informed. If you ran an analysis, explain what changed because of it. Technical skill is common at this level. Showing that your analysis moved something measurable is what separates strong candidates from average ones.
- Show range across the full analytics process. The strongest candidates can speak to data collection, cleaning, modeling, visualization, stakeholder communication, and follow-through. Even if your experience leans heavier in one of these areas, demonstrating awareness of the full picture makes you look more capable and more senior than your title might suggest.
- Avoid the generic-resume trap. One of the biggest mistakes we see is resumes that read like they were sent to every analyst opening on the market with no adjustments. Even a strong background gets passed over when the language is too broad to match what a specific employer is actually trying to solve.
- Make your cross-functional collaboration obvious. Data analyst roles, especially remote ones, succeed or fail on how well someone communicates and partners across teams. Concrete examples of working with operations, finance, product, or leadership go further than generic mentions of "collaboration."
- Quantify your contributions wherever possible. Candidates consistently undersell their impact. If your work helped reduce reporting time, improve forecasting accuracy, increase visibility into a key metric, or surface an opportunity worth real money, that should be front and center, with numbers attached.
- Recognize how much time gets wasted on the wrong opportunities. In the current market, a lot of strong analysts spend hours applying to roles that are stalled, overcrowded, or no longer a true priority for the company. Focusing your effort on roles that are clearly active and aligned is one of the highest-leverage things you can do during a search.
- Practice explaining technical work in plain language. Many analysts can describe their work to other analysts but struggle when a hiring manager or executive asks them to walk through a project. If you can explain what you analyzed, why it mattered, and what changed because of it, in three or four clean sentences, you will outperform most of the other candidates you are competing with.

These are some of the most notable points that continue to come up as we work through candidate evaluations for this role and others like it. We hope this gives you a clearer sense of what to expect and what to focus on.
We appreciate your patience and will continue to keep you updated as things progress.

Hi Netanya, Thank you for applying to Principal. We’re always looking for talent who bring unique perspectives, passion, and expertise to help us advance the financial security and well-being of our customers. We’re glad you’re considering us for your next role. With your application complete for the following job, here’s what you can expect as next steps. Analyst, Data Management (2026-50992) - Timing – Generally, you’ll hear from us within two weeks of your application unless otherwise noted in the job posting. - Communication – A member of our Talent Team will share updates and decisions either via email or phone call throughout your candidacy. If your application does not meet the minimum qualifications for the position, you will receive an email within the next few days. - Interviewing – Depending on the position, we’ll conduct interviews through a combination of methods including over the phone, video, through pre-recorded video/audio technology, or face to face. To help you prepare, check out our "How we hire" page on our Career Site. - Decisions – If the decision is made to move forward with other candidates (which could be for a variety of reasons), you'll receive an email from us. For future reference throughout the application process, the text from the job posting is provided near the bottom of this email.     As always, you can view the status of your application at any time.   Login: netanyakelley6@gmail.com (If you do not know your password, you can reset it here.)   If you would like to update any of your EEO information (gender and/or race), you may click https://tracking.icims.com/f/a/Rg61lfvXZ3tF8TVtevOk6g~~/AAIB5hA~/MzICKlG-v8P02A0nsRdK0mwD9CATVNd6MR6vMF1k_hualsve7F-5D6SFlx7vF_8ZLz0ipHUUGzt0BqmfyLYPi78DBqCKpsDX0iBRA6BlSRS53t4RtmBVG24rIjvOJWGHef4DGeEbvl0vJ7qqJcmomw~~ log in and access that data.       At Principal, we invest in what matters. And building talented teams is where it all begins. Explore our careers site to learn more about what makes Principal a great place to work.   Job posting text... What You'll Do:

Independently complete daily operations, perform data analysis, and fulfill ad hoc requests to ensure high-quality, reliable data and accurate sales attribution across the global sales lifecycle. The team operates in a fast-paced environment that places an emphasis on continuous learning, collaboration, and maintaining an equitable and fun working environment.

 

    • Collect, validate, and consolidate data from various sources to support research, data governance, resolve inquiries, and correct errors. Maintain data integrity and security across systems, handle exception requests, and provide operational support for projects, and processes in diverse operational environments.
    • Contribute to distribution efforts through involvement in projects, process reviews, and system adjustments. Take proactive steps to recognize and manage challenges by evaluating and finding operational improvements that uphold accurate and reliable data handling and processing during the sales lifecycle.
    • Collaborate with internal and external personnel, which may include senior operations staff, client reporting, performance, accounting, sales, marketing, finance, IT, vendors, portfolio managers, traders, and analysts to collect information and work together on resolving issues.
    • Provide guidance, training, and mentorship to team members while demonstrating an ability to share knowledge with others.

 

Operating at the intersection of financial services and technology, Principal builds financial tools that help our customers live better lives. We take pride in being a purpose-led firm, motivated by our mission to make financial security accessible to all. Our mission, integrity, and customer focus have made us a trusted leader for more than 140 years!  

  Who You Are:
  • A Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in accounting, finance, economics, or business. Experience in Data Analytics and Data Governance is required.
  • 1+ years of professional experience in investment or mutual fund operations, or a related area, is preferred.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, interpersonal, time management, and communication abilities.
  • High level of precision and carefulness with the capability to deliver accurate and timely information.
  • Capability to handle various tasks simultaneously in a dynamic setting with urgent deadlines and minimal direct oversight.
  • Strong ability to prioritize and adapt as business needs evolve.
  • Ability to build strong working relationships, show flexibility, and effectively interact with internal and external contacts at all levels.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.

 

We are also open to hiring at the next level, if the candidate has all the qualifications above, as well as the additional listed below. The Associate, Data Management role is exempt.

Associate, Data Management

In this position, data governance will play a central role, requiring collaboration both within the business unit and across the broader organization. This emphasis ensures that governance initiatives receive robust representation, consistent support and implementation.

  • 2+ years of experience in investment or mutual fund operations or a related area.
  • Experience with financial tools and systems such as Salesforce, Power BI, and SQL query.

Hi Netanya,

Thanks for applying to the Junior Credit Analyst role we shared recently. Your background looks strong, and we’d love for you to take the next step: a short AI-led interview (6-10 minutes). This will cover topics like your recent jobs, challenges and tools you use and will be visible to the Employer.

This employer requires candidates to use our interviewing platform (Calyptus!) for initial screening stages. Here are the next steps to take: 
1. Apply directly via this link: 👉🏼 https://www.calyptus.co/jobs?slug=gWbuJojgfH
2. Complete a short AI Interview - select the Interview when prompted - (5-10minutes)
3. Showcase the real you (and stand out above a LinkedIn application)
4. Have your video application reviewed by the employer
5. Appear in dozens of other candidates searches by our Clients !

Once complete, our team will review your interview and get in touch about next steps. You’ll also gain a Calyptus profile, which means other employers on the platform can discover you and reach out directly.

The sooner you complete the interview, the better your chances.

However you can delete your profile after some time if you prefer. It is not public, it is only viewable to our clients. The client is actively viewing the platform and this process should take two weeks to conclude.

If you have completed the AI interview recently, you do not need to do it again.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

Thank you!

Best,
Nicole
